plan.title: Entropy Explained: Why Time Only Runs One Way
plan.description: Entropy measures how many ways a system can be arranged, and why nature drifts toward the most likely arrangements. This explainer covers the second law, the myth that order can never appear, and why time seems to have an arrow.

beats.narration: Why does milk spread into coffee but never separate again? Why does ice melt, but a puddle never freezes itself? Nature has a one-way direction, and it has a name: entropy.
Entropy is a measure of how many ways the parts of a system can be arranged without changing what you see. More arrangements means higher entropy.

props.definition: A measure of how many ways the parts of a system can be arranged without changing what you see.

beats.narration: Think of a deck of cards. Only one order is perfectly sorted. But there are astronomically many shuffled orders. Shuffle, and you almost surely land in a messy one.
That is why a tidy room drifts toward mess. There are few ways to be tidy and endless ways to be messy. Disorder is simply far more likely.
Heat works the same way. Hot coffee shares its energy with the cooler air, spreading it out. Energy spreads until everything is the same temperature.
This is the second law of thermodynamics: in an isolated system, entropy tends to increase over time. It is a law of probability, backed by overwhelming odds.

props.text: In an isolated system, entropy tends to increase over time.

beats.narration: Common myth: entropy means disorder, so order can never appear. But a fridge cools food and life builds order. They do it by exporting more disorder as heat elsewhere.

props.heading: Myth versus fact
items: Cost: more disorder as heat elsewhere

beats.narration: Entropy also gives time its arrow. A film of shattering glass run backward looks wrong because that never happens. The past is the lower-entropy direction.
Even the universe follows it. Stars burn fuel and pour heat into space. That flow from concentrated to spread out is what lets engines, and living things, do work.
Entropy counts how many ways things can be arranged, and systems drift toward the most likely arrangements. Look around: spilled, melted, cooled, mixed. That is entropy at work.
